subject: Urgent: production p95/p99 spike + 429 cascade — FastRetail impact
messages:
From: Carla Ortega <carla.ortega@fastretail.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: dan.infra@fastretail.com, support@fastretail.com
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Production: p95/p99 spike + 429 cascade (impacting checkout)

Jonas —

We're seeing a severe degradation in our checkout flow starting ~08:50 PST this morning. p95 latency for Redwood hosted generation endpoints has jumped from ~240ms to ~2.3s and p99 is above 6s. Concurrently, our frontend is getting a wave of 429s from your API and our retry logic is amplifying client-side traffic — we're observing a retry burst that correlates with a backlog of long requests and then timeouts from our side. This is directly impacting checkout throughput (orders/sec down ~18%).

Attached two quick artifacts: a synthetic p95/p99 graph and a short sample of client retry logs. We need immediate mitigation: can Redwood temporarily increase their soft rate limit for our account, or open burst capacity to get us back to baseline while we stabilize client retry logic?

Please treat this as urgent — we're prepared to join a bridge immediately. CC'ing Dan (infra) and support.

Thanks,
Carla Ortega
VP Engineering, FastRetail, Inc.

Subject: Re: Production: p95/p99 spike + 429 cascade (impacting checkout)

Carla / team — initial findings from the runtime telemetry:

Summary:
- Between 08:45 and 09:10 PST we observed a burst of requests from the FastRetail account to redwood-chat-xl-v2 with high token-length variance. The serving runtime's soft per-account rate limiter started returning 429s as the in-flight queue grew.
- Many client retries (no jitter + immediate retry) appear to have contributed to a tight feedback loop: retries increased instantaneous QPS which increased queueing and latency, producing more 429s/timeouts.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional pools fast enough because the burst pattern had spikes shorter than our scale-up cooldown (configured 120s), and the kernel selection step had CPU hot-spots for long-sequence requests.

Short-term mitigations applied (09:30 PST):
- Temporary soft-limit increase for FastRetail (rolled to 2x) — monitoring backlog drain now.
- Enabled an emergency fallback route to redwood-chat-medium-v1 for new non-critical calls (we're routing non-checkout telemetry/preview calls).
- Flipped a quiesce for long-seq requests to reduce kernel contention (low-risk).

Requested actions from FastRetail:
- If possible, add jitter/backoff to retry logic (exponential backoff with randomized jitter). We can provide a small client patch suggestion.
- Share a couple of representative request IDs (we have partial traces) so we can correlate traces end-to-end.

Attachments I pushed to the internal drive: hosted-api-traces-0222.zip (contains span snippets), plus a short excerpt of the 429 timeline (attached here as text).

We're continuing to monitor. If the backlog doesn't clear in the next 15–20 minutes we'll open dedicated capacity for the account.

— Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Carla / FastRetail execs —

Thanks for working through the incident with us today. Quick executive summary and actions we opened:

What happened (short):
- A short, high-variance burst of long-sequence generation calls to redwood-chat-xl-v2 created queueing pressure on a subset of serving hosts. Per-account soft-rate limits began returning 429s; client retries without jitter amplified the burst and produced tail latency regressions. Autoscaling cooldowns prevented immediate pool growth.

What we did (tactical):
- Opened an emergency soft-limit increase (2x) and temporary fallback routing to redwood-chat-medium-v1 for lower-priority calls — backlog cleared to baseline by ~10:20 PST.
- Applied a short quiesce for long-sequence kernel paths to reduce contention.
- SRE put a hold on scale-down for the next 4 hours and created INF-2210 to track follow-ups.

Next (short-term) commitments:
- We'll keep soft-limit increase in place until EOD PST (can be extended by request).
- Rishi and team will provide a small client-side retry pattern doc (recommended jitter/backoff).
- Marissa will own the credit request and coordinate with Finance; I'll escalate to our revenue ops for a goodwill credit review.

Follow-up exec sync: Mon 2026-02-23 10:00 PST — 30m (invite to follow). I'd like to include our head of platform and FastRetail's infra lead.

If you'd like us to open dedicated capacity for steady-state headroom while you deploy retry fixes, we can scope X-week reserved capacity options and a short-term emergency capacity surcharge.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take availability seriously and will run a post-incident RCA.

Jonas Weber
